memory_update.text: LOPE is the cleanest direct public-market mapping for the online higher-education fixed-cost stack because it explicitly provides enrollment, student services, SIS support, marketing, curriculum, and faculty support to university partners.

NNI should be tracked as an underfollowed infrastructure candidate because its loan-servicing identity may obscure education technology, payments, financial management, and student/school information system exposure.

COUR belongs in the universe as a platform and credential-distribution layer, but later layers must distinguish durable university infrastructure revenue from consumer course demand and lower-retention enterprise revenue.

LRN is a speculative-shadow candidate for this specific node: strong online learning/career-learning relevance, but higher-education fixed-cost-stack exposure is less direct and must be verified by segment and customer evidence.
The node appears investable through service-stack providers, education payments/SIS vendors, credential platforms, and online career-learning operators rather than through universities alone.

Many true SIS, LMS, and OPM assets are private or recently taken private; later passes should check whether any public micro/small-cap vendors remain in niche admissions CRM, proctoring, accreditation, simulation labs, or healthcare education workflow software.

node: Online higher-education fixed-cost stack: enrollment marketing, student services, course development, and student-information systems
summary: Expanded the universe around the fixed-cost operating stack needed to launch and scale online higher-education and workforce programs. The underfollowed lane is strongest where public companies provide enrollment management, student lifecycle support, student-information/payment systems, course/curriculum infrastructure, or university-facing credential platforms rather than simply owning schools. The best-fit candidates for this pass are Grand Canyon Education, Nelnet, Coursera, and Stride. Grand Canyon Education is the closest pure-play service-provider match; Nelnet is a less obvious infrastructure/payments/SIS angle; Coursera is a university and employer credential platform with degree and campus exposure; Stride is a second-order online learning and career-training infrastructure name, but its K-12 weighting means the higher-ed fixed-cost link needs more verification.
